events.name: Ecological Initiative
events.description:
With God Programs, more specifically Anubis, gone, the responsibility of their duties fell back on humanity once more, and while in a lot of cases their functionality was rerouted or essentially taken over by other organizations, in some cases, such as environmental duties, they started to become heavily neglected. Anubis was meant to be used for ecological preservation, and yet with most infrastructure lost, the whole left by the program began to become apparent to Hector and Claudio. The Martins were long time environmentalist advocates, and they believed that Overwatch could be used to improve the world, so they took a proposal to Morrison and the UN to create a specialized Watchpoint branch. 

The Ecopoint Program would create stations staffed with Overwatch's scientific leads in critical locations across the globe, where they could monitor ongoing abnormalities in nature and aid in global efforts for preservation of the environment. In spite of a wave of nationalism and distrust for Overwatch presence hitting many countries over the years, the Ecopoints were quite a welcomed proposal, as the Martins were highly respected names in the international communities they worked with, and the benefits of scientifically-oriented bases were far more self-evident than the more generalist and often military nature of Watchpoints. With the approval of the program, other big names like Mui and Namuaca quickly joined, adding further credibility to the initiative. In the end, seven initial bases were approved, with more coming later.

Biosphere (Green) Ecopoints:
- Ecopoint: Antartica focused on monitoring the impacts of climate change and pursuing methods of recovery of both the atmosphere and the ice caps, as well as studying strange fluctuations found around the Peninsula. 
- Ecopoint: Connemara focused on the restoration of Irish boglands, later on collaborating with Russian scientists to aid in revitalizing the Siberian lowlands. 
- Ecopoint: Tarapoto, deep within the Colombian Amazon, was built to study the many ecosystems of the area. 
- Ecopoint: Osa in Costa Rica would focus on the recovery of reptiles and amphibians of the Corcovado cloud forest, seen as a bellwether of the rest of the natural world, focusing primarily on antifungals and biological solutions to waste treatment. 

Hydrosphere (Blue) Ecopoints:
- Samoa would receive a base within one of the active volcanoes, to focus on seismic monitoring and geothermal research, detecting multiple major earthquakes in the region and saving countless lives. 
- Ecopoint: Zealandia off the coast of New Zeland would exist in response to the Australian fall-out zone, focusing on filtering radiation and aiding in the recovery of Oceania following the ALF's attack. 
- And lastly, Ecopoint: Monterrey, a submarine base off the shore of California, meant to research marine life and follow protocols originally proposed by Leon Honisch to aid in the recovery of many species. The program was overall seen as one of Overwatch's most clean-cut successes and net positives to society at large, and a great example of the good they could do for the world

While the scientists were often busy with their duties at the base, they made an active effort to give Juno a happy and healthy childhood, but it was clear their curiosity rubbed off on the young girl. Having been born in an early colony with so few people, in a world so far away from Earth, Juno was quite sheltered and inexperienced with a lot of the ways the world worked, things that would be normal to an Earth-born human were completely alien and often terrifying for her.

It also meant that Juno was always eager to get out there, and see more of her home. She wanted to help the team join in expeditions on the planet's surface, and once she was old enough, they would provide her with her own space suit, allowing her to roam through the outdoors of the colony and aid the scientists on the staff, as a true member of the team. events.name: Omnic Rights
events.description:
The decade following the crisis saw the rise of the Omnic Rights movement, as it became clear to the world as a whole that the sentience was permanent and impossible to ignore, and Omnics themselves grappled with their place in the world. While cities like Toronto and Numbani made active efforts towards Omnic integration, the reality is that the world at large was generally far more hostile. From the cleansing of Ravager units, to the destruction of the Australian Omnium, or the inhospitable conditions of the London Underworld, to domestic units being thrown into the streets all over the planet, as their previous families rejected them or in worse cases, were forced back into servitude. Something needed to change, and here, so an organized movement began to campaign for the United Nations, seeking for global recognition of rights and obligations for all Omnics, to be treated with equal respect and empathy as humans.

When the UN finally took a stance on the issue, Liao was called as a witness for the case of Omnic sentience. In the hearings she brought in the research and records she had performed while under Ovewatch, alongside previous evidence used for Aurora's original case. In response to the mountains of undeniable evidence, the UN agreed and granted Omnic kind legal personhood status worldwide. In spite of this, not every government complied, and many humans would continue to resent and discriminate Omnic communities. Cases like Cliff Brassey, the first human charged for Omnic Murder, echo the feelings of many people around the world: "Breaking a machine is property damage, isn't it? This'll blow over. We'll put the tin cans back in the kitchen and forget this ever happened."
The road towards equality would be a long and dragged out one, but progress was possible, and more than welcomed.

While Overwatch's reputation and support was still high across the world, over the last couple of of years they have experienced a series of rejections. Korea refused the establishment of a Watchpoint: in Busan, then Numbani chose to remain outside of jurisdiction in spite of Doomfist's attacks. Reyes and Cassidy would begin a crackdown on criminals in Calgary, Chicago and Saint Paul. And during this time, a drug trafficker would raise a lawsuit in his defense, arguing Overwatch had no authority over living humans, only Omnics. Naturally, this was quickly dismissed and seen as an attempt to extort money and avoid prosecution, but the red tape and politics of it all slowed Overwatch down. After the crisis, a mission came up that would allow Morrison to put Overwatch's charter to a test. The family of an American diplomat had been kidnapped and taken into Russia, and Morrison tasked Amari to retrieve her. Ana sidestepped protocol and did the mission before Russia approved of her clearance. Everything went well. She tracked down the terrorist and retrieved the civilians alive, but in the end, she was intercepted by the Russian government and charged with illegal entering and obstruction of local law enforcement. Ana was released, but permanently banned from Russia.

This would not be the only time Overwatch broke protocol. An incident in Cape Town led to a rouge god program to escape containment and rebel against its captors, catching the attention of Anubis loyalists and forming an insurrection, but the red tape stopped Morrison from sending in any troops. Lucky for him, Lacroix had extensive covert ops training and came up with the idea of sending both him and Reyes "on vacation." The pair had a quiet trip, limiting themselves to intel gathering and evacuation of sources, as well as, on the rare occasion, the disappearance of one or two criminals. Coincidentally, their vacation led to the apprehension of the rouge AI and the loyalist suddenly vanished, all without official Overwatch involvement. Following this success and the repeated tension with international bureaucracy, Morrison would approve of more and more vacations between the Blackwatch staff, Cassidy joining them in many cases, but whether Jack knew the full extent of these trips is unknown.

events.name: Growing with the Clan
events.description:
Over the years, the Shimada family had come to rely on the Yamagami Blades, the business run by Toshiro and his wife, Asa. The Yamagami name has served the city for generations following traditional paths, heavily linked by the local shrine to the Fox Spirit, and now under Shimada control, the family chose their side in the turf war of the clans. Not only did Toshiro develop the Anima weapons used by the clean head and his sons, but his wife proved to be quite an asset as well. Often regarded as the best sword master in the world, Asa would serve as the teacher to the Shimada brothers. From a very young age, Asa wished for his daughter to also choose the path of the blade, so since she was very little, Kiriko would often join the brothers in training. Both brothers would quickly grow attached to the little girl, seeing her as a little niece figure. Genji in particular, was one to slack off from training and play with the kids, stealing sweets from the kitchen and playing games in the arcade.

 It was not just the brothers who Kiriko grew close to, since she spent so much time in the Shimada Castle, the clan leader, Sojiro Shimada had also grown accustomed to her presence. She would often join the family during the fireworks festivals at the end of summer, and during one night, he told his sons the stories of the clan. How centuries ago, a rival clan attempted to end their rule by setting the orchards aflame, but the Shimada did not move to defend the fields. Instead, they aided the people. These teachings heavily shaped Kiriko's perspective of the clan as Kanezaka's protectors, while she was still too young to understand the true nature of their operations.

On the off days when Kiriko was not training, she spent time at the Fox shrine with her grandmother, who taught her the traditional ways of spiritual cleansing and meditation. From an early age, her grandmother would teach him how to use the Anima ofuda that her dad had crafted, to summon the Fox spirit and use it to aid those in need. Much like how her mother wanted her to follow in her footsteps, her grandma had laid another path for her as well.

events.name: Pocket King
events.description:
Following the Crisis many Omnics struggled to integrate into human society. Very few of them managed to climb up the ladder of capitalism, but perhaps there is no bigger success than that of Maximillien. Before the crisis, Max was a low-level accountant in Marseille, but following the Awakening he found himself in the position of a preeminent financial advisor for La Coterie, the name the press had given to a group of Europe's most influential power brokers. While he was often stepped on by many of his clients, soon enough they all began kneeling at his feet.  For the longest time, his clients blindly trusted their assets into Max, and behind their backs he had built an elaborate web of money laundering and contingency agreements, very carefully worded deals that would all direct those fortunes directly to him. After years of serving ignorant, arrogant Tycoons, Max arranged a meeting with the six most powerful figures of Monaco, and broke to them the news; he owned each one of them and their companies. 

Overnight, Max had become one of the most powerful figures in out of Europe, and the head of La Coterie. The Omnic was one call away from bankrupting anyone he wished to, so his old clients had no real choice but to serve him. Over the years, Maximillien had guided the reconstruction and rise of Monte Carlo from the shadows, and after years of effort he owned half of the city. His reign over Monaco would continue to expand as he pursued other deals across Europe and beyond, later acquiring Don Rumbotico in Cuba and using it as yet another front for his money laundering. From the window views of his casino, Max watched as the world's wealthiest and powerful elites fed from his hand.

events.name: Valkirie
events.description:
It had been ten years since the end of the Crisis, and Angela's early career was already a fruitful one. Her breakthroughs in the field of applied nanobiology radically improved the treatment of life-threatening injuries, capable of stabilizing near-death patients and saving countless lives. Through her schooling and early years outside of college, Overwatch kept an eye on her, allowing her access to the Watchpoints as she volunteered on the medical staff. Ziegler's technology could have made her rich if she chose to remain in private practice, but she always saw science as something that belonged to the world and the people who benefited from it.

It was here when Morrison finally chose to approach her directly. As the world finally moved away from the crisis, Morrison wished to shift towards peacetime and civilian applications. The heavy investment in the support departments and Ecopoint bases was one of the early signs of this new mission, making the world a better place. As such, Morrison offered Angela to become the leader of the medical division, with all the money, resources and personnel she could ever dream of. Angela was intrigued by these promises, but she was greatly opposed to the militaristic nature of Overwatch. Even since losing her parents to the war, she did not have the greatest opinion on military peacekeeping.

In the end, she had agreed to the offer with one caveat. The same way Torbjörn requested back in the day, she wanted to become a part of the strike team, so she could keep a level of control over the use of her technology and allow her to see at work personally. Morrison agreed. In order to work on the frontlines, she began development of the Valkyrie swift-response suit, a personal aerial combat armor that came equipped with nanobiotic capabilities and assistive protocols. Ziegler quickly proved to be a surprisingly adept field agent, with a surgical tactic approach to changing situations. Between her efficiency and the design of her suit, she quickly gained notoriety among the strike team, earning her the call sign "Mercy". While she did not enjoy the way this framed her, she was always glad to use her technology for the greater good.

events.name: Deep Rising
events.description:
Not long after the Gwishin attack, Overwatch received another emergency call from Busan. The Colossus had reappeared, larger than before and upgraded with new abilities. Overwatch dispatched all available agents, but even then, the tactics they used the previous time were no longer effective against it, and the team continued to struggle in maritime battles, so as the giant approached the coastline they were forced to evacuate the city. Fortunately, at the time, the strike team had grown rapidly, and new agents like Fusionator and Soundquake played a big role in defeating the Gwishin. The new agents had not faced the Gwishin before, yet their unique abilities proved effective when everything else failed. They were able to distract the colossus long enough for the rest of the team to take it down.

Mina Liao would be joined by Dr. Yi-am Lim, a robotics engineer from the Korean military. They both analyzed the footage and concluded the warbot was an upgraded version of that of the previous attack, but everyone wondered how that would be possible. It would require an entire team of the best engineers to get this machine running again after years, yet the timeline did not add up. Artificial Intelligence must have been involved in the accelerated development, and everyone began fearing the worst. Liao's research team was dispatched to the Temple of Anubis, to determine if the rouge AI had managed to escape containment, but they found no breaching happened. The researchers were astounded by trying to look for a source, when the third attack happened.

The colossus reemerged from the water, evolved yet again with a design that directly countered Soundquake's technology. Thanks to Dr Lim and yet another new agent, Rumble, the team was able to identify weak points and defeat the machine quicker, and with a smaller force this time. The swift response allowed Lim's team to retrieve the wreckage before the warbot dived back into the water. Thanks to this, they discovered the Gwishin had not been built in any known Omnium. Overwatch scouted the local sea floor and found a series of small drones lurking in the depths, attacking the diving team and forcing them to retreat. The only logical conclusion Liao could reach was that somewhere in the depths of the East China Sea, there was a secret Omnium, likely built by Anubis, and possibly it was not the only one. In spite of their combined efforts and Lim's wishes, Korea chose to remain independent in this battle, and Overwatch left after sharing their findings, despite Liao's frustration with the government choosing politics over allowing Overwatch to protect their people.

events.name: Takeover
events.description:
For years, Akande Ogundimu had trained under the wing of Akinjide Adeyemi, as one of the best lieutenants. His involvement was known by Numbani's security forces, but he was smart enough to keep distance away from more active conflicts to avoid being apprehended. As Ogundimu became one of Adeyemi's most trusted confidants, behind his back, Akande was thinking far bigger than he could ever have imagined. Akande was a well-studied visionary, who had grown to adopt a certain philosophy as his personal mantra: Humanity evolves through conflict.  =It was conflict like the pandemics earlier in the century that pushed medical advances to their limits. It was conflict like the ecological impact of humanity that led to the hundreds of inventions that made life better. It was a conflict like the Omnic Crisis that allowed humanity to come together with Overwatch, and push through an enemy larger than any nation on their own. It was conflict that prevented him from sports, and allowed him to realize his true calling. Akande was meant to spread conflict across the world, for the betterment of humanity.

Akande had grown connections within Talon's council through Adeyemi's network of mercenaries, and within the council they saw him as a potentially valuable asset. Before long, Ogundimu made his choice. He turned against his master and after a brutal face off, he was able to kill him, taking the Gauntlet and the mantle of Doomfist for himself. Akande was already respected within Talon, but between his vision, and now the imposing force of the Gauntlet, the members of the council would have little option but to fall in line at his command. After all, it would be easier to take advantage of governments and industry amid the chaos of ongoing conflicts, so while the new Doomfist pursued an ideology, his closest allies stuck around purely to profit from his crusade.

Under Doomfist, Talon would shift from being an amorphous, silent force that hijacked power across regions, to a loud, imposing terrorist that quickly proved to be Overwatch's primary obstacle in their peacekeeping duties. The organization was actively growing at this time as well. Research teams began to raise warnings of fringe scientists being recruited by Talon agents, and in some cases, reputable researchers getting kidnapped. Perhaps a more direct blow would be the beggining of a recruitment campaign across the Carribean Sea, as many experienced personnel from the Caribbean Coalition ranks began to be lured by the calling of Talon. Reyes and Lacroix became aware of the change in leadership and even obtained partial footage of the battle. The subject became a main priority for their research, but soon enough, Overwatch would have their hands full from dealing with Talon.

events.name: Lost in Time
events.description:
Overwatch's research team was relatively quieter than the many controversies the Strike team and Blackwatch would eventually be remembered for, but one of their many experiments would become one of the things the organization became the most known for. Lena Oxton was at the time a young pilot in the Brittish Royal Air Force and had just enlisted into Overwatch for trials of their next generation, teleporting fighter jet, the Splitstream. Lena might have been pretty young at the time, but her uniquely fast reflexes, hand coordination and love for flying at high speeds made her the most suited choice for the test that Britain could offer. 

Unfortunately, during the first test flight, the ship's teleportation matrix would malfunction, and suddenly both Oxton and the jet vanished. Lena was presumed dead, and the incident did not bring any good publicity for Overwatch, but what the scientists did not expect at the time was that Lena's disappearance was a far more complex, rare event than merely vanishing in the accident.

Oxton's molecular structure had become desynchronized from the regular flow of time and space, a condition that would later be called "Chronal Disassociation." In short, Lena was a living ghost, disappearing for hours and days at a time, and whenever she was visible in our present, it was often at completely different places, and she could barely maintain a physical form for long. Lena would remain in this limbo state for about two whole years, in which her body showed no signs of aging while disassociated from our timeline. After her first reappearance in the months after the accident, Shira Wexler, the lead designer of the jet, took full responsibility for her condition and dedicated her team's efforts to finding a cure.

To make matters easier, the Clan had also lost their other heir, not long after Genji. Hanzo Shimada had abandoned his duties, feeling ashamed by his actions, since, as far as he knew, he had killed his brother in cold blood at the orders of a bunch of old men who were supposed to serve him. They say the man became a vagabond, taking his father's Anima storm bow with him as a memento, he swore never to wield a blade again, and once he left Hanamura Castle and began to travel the world, seeking for ways to restore his honor and put his old life behind.

The long-lasting Shimada Clan had been completely dismantled from the shadows, and although Genji craved more, and actively pursued the take-down of other rival gangs in the region like the Hashimoto, the conditions that allowed for the fall of the Shimada were ultimately too circumstantial. events.name: Cold Snap
events.description:
Shortly after O'Deorain's recruitment, Overwatch would face a devastating loss in Ecopoint: Antartica. The scientific team on the base dedicated their studies to finding and replicating anomalous weather conditions, but not even with their equipment and knowledge were they able to foresee the quick formation of a massive superstorm in the region. An abnormally huge blizzard trapped the team within the base in unlivable conditions, and made evacuation efforts extremely risky. The Ecopoint facilities were equipped with cryo sleep technology, allowing the team to freeze their bodies and enter a stasis, which should have allowed them to survive until the storm passed. These kinds of storms had happened before, and it had become standard procedure, but this particular blizzard was worse than any projections could have estimated.

As the storm raged on, the team remained in cryo stasis, getting past the survival time window, where the system should have forced them to wake up, in the middle of the never-ending blizzard. Months passed, and the storm did not dissipate. Any attempts to establish communication failed, so the team was pressured to death. Overwatch would attempt to retrieve their bodies on multiple occasions, but the storm's anomalous persistence prevented access to the base for a full year. During one of the many rescue attempts, an Icebreaker ship, the Resolute, would crash into the Ice, and the rescue team barely managed to escape with their lives. The anomaly continued and Overwatch was forced to stop further retrieval attempts, lest they lose more agents.

All of Overwatch entered a mourning period, with the Ecopoint bases rushing to improve security protocols in case of evacuation, and the UN calling for a full accounting of the records for review. Hector and Claudio joined their old partners in mourning the loss of the entire Antarctica team, and those who died trying to get their bodies back.

events.name: Deep Sea Raiders
events.description:
While the Ecopoints helped alleviate ecological concerns across the globe, not every nation was too keen on pushing environmentalist standards. Both corporate greed and sometimes even plain irresponsibility by well-meaning people got in the way. The super coral had successfully helped rejuvenate several coral trees across the Pacific, but it was far too effective. It kept expanding across the world's oceans, and as they continued to feed off of pollutants, they began to grow out of proportion, emerging out of the water into sharp structures comparable to small islands.

For many nations, these super coral reefs serve as another source of tourism and national pride, obvious to the true implications of an introduced species becoming so dominant. For businesses across the globe, however, the reefs blocked trade routes and made it difficult for boats to navigate across many different regions of the planet, disrupting trade globally. Because of their impact, many companies began to equip boats with means to break through the reefs, and some of the people of the Polynesian nations took to this as a personal insult to their culture and history. 

The Deep-sea Raiders came to call themselves activists who battled capitalism and took curving fossil fuel emissions into their own hands, but in reality they were little more than Eco-terrorists. The pirates would hijack many boats crossing near their territories, kill the tribulation, and then steer the ships to crash into the coral which would feed off the oil and debris, growing even larger than they would normally. The Polynesian League was naturally directly impacted by the Deep-sea Raider activity, which disrupted the ecological balance and worsened business relationships with other nations. The league sought to deal with these raiding cells swiftly, but they proved to be quite a persistent movement, supported by a lot of locals who saw this as the government turning back on their culture and the wishes of their people, in spite of the irreparable damage that their harsh actions caused.

events.name: Escalation
events.description:
Null Sector activity continued across the world, inspiring many Omnics to follow Ramattra's teachings, especially following the groundbreaking of Turing Green, which many followers of Mondatta saw as a new start for Omnics. Null Sector, in contrast, took the idea as an insult, throwing a bone at his people to try and act like it absolved them from years worth of injustice. As momentum grew, the group radicalized from a small cell of liberators, to a fully militarized operation. The escalation meant many of his initial supporters soon began to leave the group behind, but his resolve to bring justice for all Omnics only grew stronger with each ally he lost.

He decided to bring his closest allies, Nameless, Zera and Lanet, on a journey across the depths of a freezing wasteland, where they found the very same Anubis made Omnium, where Ramattra was born. His plan was to use the facility to create an army, and use it to speak to humans in a language they can understand, violence. For the next two years, the group would produce entire battalions of Crisis-era units at Lanet's supervision, and Ramattra himself would upgrade his own design combining Shambali technology with an invention of his own, Nanites, microscopic machines capable of cooperation and assembly of different structures, including extra reinforced limbs for close combat. As his army grew, Ramattra already had his eyes on the first target of his revolution, but Lanet urged caution, noting the antiquated designs needed more work if they wanted to get things right.

During this back-and-forward, tension built up over philosophical differences amongst the group, as Ramattra continuously refused to involve other Omnics and rally forces outside his mindless troops. While Nameless and Zera were used to appealing to the Omnic masses, and wished to allow their people to fight alongside them, Ramattra was tired of bloodshed. He saw himself as a liberator, not a general. It was because of this that he chose to manufacture an army of robots, instead of using his influence to command his supporters, as he wished to keep sentient Omnics away from active conflict as much as possible. This led to constant argument with his allies, who saw their leader radicalize further into a lonely crusade.

Winston's reception was mixed at the start due to the ethically questionable nature of his mere existence, but he quickly proved to be an invaluable ally for the organization, as well as one of the most charismatic faces of the Strike team, becoming the face of the "Overwatch Adventures" cartoon, and by far the most marketable agent with a line of pluses and toys of his own.

events.name: Chronal Dissociation
events.description:
Overwatch generally saw Winston as a possible fresh start, an outsider who had no preconceptions about Omnics, and with an idealized vision of human culture and history. He never saw the world for what it was, he dared to see what it could be. Since he lacked the assumptions of what was or not possible, he was the perfect mind to tackle the Oxton case. Alongside Wexler's team, Winston studied Lena's Chronal disassociation condition and began work on a device that he called the Chronal anchor. This harness was intended to pull Oxton back into the normal flow of time, and keep her from blipping out again. However, when tested, the device was only capable of keeping Lena anchored in space, not time. Her body was no longer reappearing in entirely different places, but it still vanished from the time flow uncontrollably. Still, progress was still progress.

During this testing, Winston realized that the matrix of the device was building up an unknown form of energy the longer Lena was kept anchored. Eventually, this buildup reaches a critical amount, causing Oxton's time fluctuations. After learning this, he scrapped the original design in favor of a new device called the Chronal Accelerator. This new iteration harnessed the mounting energy into a limited, controlled disassociation, essentially allowing Oxton to experience localized time travel at will. The device kept Lena anchored in time, and as energy built, she could use it to willingly blink or rewind back her own relationship with time and space, releasing the buildup without losing control. Oxton was stable and capable of living a somewhat normal life as long as she was in proximity to a Chronal Accelerator, but she realized that this gift of hers could be used to help Overwatch and the world. So, after being cleared from test runs, Lena began training to become part of the Strike team alongside Winston, who she grew to be close friends with. After all the time, he worked on a solution to her problem. Due to the trails of light left by the Chronal accelerator as she blinked through time, she would earn the call sign Tracer.

Mauga's father was the leader of the Samoan branch of the Deepsea Raiders, and from an early age, his cell took Mauga many of their incursions, installing on him a heavy disrespect for the law and a feeling of doing something meaningful by defying those who sought to destroy the beauty of their oceans,

During a particularly intense battle against these troops, Mauga was critically wounded. He was half dead when they found him, and his heart in no condition for recovery, so the medics saw no choice but to implant a cybernetic heart, to assist his damaged systems. Mauga survived but was forever changed by this near-death experience. The first thing he did as he woke up from surgery was choke the doctor to death. He became a local legend when he returned to Samoa, known as the two-Heart Demon. Once back home, more upgrades and surgeries awaited him to keep up with his dying heart, which eventually gave out and was replaced with another cybernetic heart. 

The machines pumping blood to his body at double the power allowed his body to increase in size massively with his metabolism, but it also made maintaining his enhancements harder. Mauga lived at the verge of death every day of his life, at the mercy of either heart possibly malfunctioning. His condition taught him a valuable lesson that defined his way of life going onward: live every day carefree, because it could be his last, and while this attitude made him out to be a careless brute to many, in reality his lack of worries just made it easier to barge in and open doors to new plans.

The more time passed since the Crisis, the more the world moved away from the heavy militarization of the years prior. Volskaya industries began to face a heavy decline in Russia. The Inti Warriors of Peru made for an intriguing exception to this trend, as there were many factors that allowed them to remain strong. For one. Solar threading was already heavily used in all of Runasapi, making the idea of enhancing your own body to be compatible with it very appealing. The Intis could now serve as providers and healers for their community, and much like the rest of the Paqarina research group, they have become synonymous with Runasapi culture.

The unwavering presence of the Intis lead to continued enlisting of the locals, and over time one of the younger recruits began to stand out. Illari Quispe Ruiz had begun the demanding Inti training from an early age, and even back then her teachers saw immense potential in her, believing she could rise up to become the strongest warrior of her time. Illari took to this prodigy status proudly, dedicating most of her free time to extensive training and answering the desires of her community, so that one day she could finally live up to the legends she grew up around. Everyone in Runasapi was rooting for their young child of the sun, and as Illari grew older and stronger, it was clear she was meant to be the greatest of them all.

Amelie was hunted by both Overwatch and local police. However, that was not the biggest of her worries. She was haunted by the way killing her own husband made her feel. Unclear if it was due to the lingering effects of the conditioning she underwent or pure euphoria from a manic episode, Amelie was fighting the urge to kill again. With little options left and intoxicated by bloodlust, Amelie ended up turning to Talon, chasing the thrill of a kill again in spite of how much it terrified her. She requested to be given training to become a marksman, and consented to participate in trials for Moira's experimental program. The genetic treatment altered Amelie's physiology to turn her into the perfect killer. Slowing down her heart, which turned her skin a pale blue color, and dulled her ability to feel human emotion. These drugs allowed Amelie to kill without remorse, and strengthened the release she felt when going for a kill.

Under Talon, Amelie would go under the name of the Widowmaker, and quickly became one of their most effective assassins, turning every kill into a performance that captivated and devastated her audience, fully embracing her murderous cravings while suppressing the painful memories or her past with a heavy supply of drugs. She retreated to the abandoned Château her family owned, where spiders became her only company. And under the alias of Danielle Guillard, she was able to live a quiet Life I'm between missions, even visiting Gérard's grave on occasion, as the mixed feelings she got from his death were something Moira never managed to fully erase.

Overwatch's conflict with Talon did not just harm their internal staff, instead several civilian casualties resulted from their many encounters, and left several jaded towards the Organization. Findlay Docherty was one of the many victims from their all-out war. Having grown poor, with a widowed father that was very disconnected about his needs, Findlay was just a young teenager looking for some support from the system. His parents were Crisis veterans and regularly got checks for their service, and even if they barely allowed them to get by, it installed in the young man a deep respect for institutions. Tired of living in poverty and neglect, however, he sought a way out, enlisting in the military to help him pay for university, convinced that he would finally find success if he played along with the systems laid out in front of him.

Not long after enlisting, he was caught in the crossfire of an Overwatch in pursuit of a Talon jet. The Overwatch drop-ship had been hit, and it crashed into the flat Findlay grew up in, killing his father and leaving him trapped in the wreckage for almost two days. Findlay miraculously survived, but was left a triple amputee, preventing him from continuing his career in the military. The government offered him very basic prostheses and pain medication alongside a monthly check, but for Findlay he was still burnt by the injustice of it all. He lost everything he had worked for, and  the system gave him the bare minimum in return. Even Overwatch themselves could not bother helping beyond a speech by Strike Commander Morrison. That day marked a shift in Findlay's output for life, as he realized that he could not count on the establishment to have his back.

Following Akande's arrest, he managed to still have some level of control over Talon, bypassing his jailers' security and allowing him to communicate from the inside of his cell. However, the true person in charge of their everyday actions was now Augusto Vialli, Antonio's successor from Venice. Under Vialli's command, Talon would retreat into the shadows once more, for no cause other than what benefited the council table's pockets. His direction led to several assassinations and massive cuts in who got to have a say at the table, as the council struggled to earn bigger pieces of an increasingly smaller pie.

La Lupa herself was well aware of the direction Talon was being taken in, and she carefully watched as Vialli left them into ruin. She had earned the respect of many of her fellow gladiators, who were ready to answer to her any command. Using these connections, she deployed an attack on Talon's palace in Venice not long after Doomfist's arrest, thinking she would get an advantage by striking Talon at their weakest point. However, the assault was a failure, and it quickly became clear her numbers were still not large enough to take Talon head on. It would take years for her to be ready for another attack, but the Wolf waited patiently for her girl to strike.

events.name: The Zurich Attack
events.description:
Having arrested their biggest enemy so far gave Overwatch a new hope that public opinion would turn around for them at last, and that the streak of failures and controversies was finally over. But in the end, that hope died when an accident inside the Zurich HQ triggered an explosion that resulted in the destruction of the entire base.

Rumors and misinformation surrounded the press following the attack, with a particularly prominent one being the mention of Reyes and Morrison getting into a physical fight, possibly having caused the accident. In reality, both of the soldiers were caught by surprise in the middle of their fight. It had not been caused by anything they had encountered before, but rather an outside force with so little evidence left it would not be discovered until years later.

While many agents did their best to rescue survivors and avoid casualties, once the rubble set in, both Reyes and Morrison had gone missing. Morrison's funeral was a big event which his family agreed he would have hated, but they had little choice given his position. Reyes, on the other hand, had a quieter private event for his family and close friends only.

Jack and Gabe were not the only major profile names to disappear following the Zurich explosion. Genji had long struggled to accept his new body, and his role as a weapon under Blackwatch. The man was at war with himself and too often felt like he was not meant to be who he had become, so he took his chance after the Zurich attack and outright left without telling anyone.

Genji's journey of self-discovery would take him to many places over the years, but he would eventually reach the Nepalese mountains, where he crossed paths with the now Tekhartha Zenyatta, currently leader of the Shambali monks. Zenyatta would see Genji's struggle with accepting his new body and the man he had become, and decided to take him as a pupil, allowing him to deconstruct himself and achieve peace with himself once more. Genji would meditate with the Monks for years, with no one on the outside ever seeing Him again. He did, however, keep in contact with Angela, who he had grown to be extremely close. Even in the remote Himalayas, he found time to write her letters and keep in contact.

events.name: The Petras Act Hearings
events.description:
Calls of disbandment had happened for years since Blackwatch came to the public eye, but not with the HQ lost and the two highest ranking agents dead, it became clear there needed to be an intervention questioning the legality of ongoing Overwatch operations. The Petras Act hearings called upon all active members, as well as some retired ones like Reinhardt and closely related individuals like San to testify about Overwatch, and while most agents generally sugar coded their experiences, Vivian Chase's testimony proved lethal for Overwatch's case. Vivian had grown to resent Overwatch's position later in its life, as individuals above her continued to disregard rules. In her own words, it only spread out the team tin, making them lose focus on their objective.

Many classified documents came to light during the hearings, and through that Reyes and LaCroix's vacations would be revealed to the world. With Jack missing, he could not defend himself and was judged as if he had been fully aware of the illegal nature of their activities. Dr. Naughton also came in to testify that her boys would have been able to survive the explosion, which only made matters worse, as now many believe they went under hiding to avoid persecution. In the end, the United Nations passed the Petras Act, to be enforced by the International Justice Committee. The act rendered all Overwatch activity illegal and stripped Agents of their credentials and equipment.

A certain private security firm had begun to make a name for itself around the Middle East, and quickly began to expand its profile internationally over the years. Helix Securities International, backed by Oasis University, quickly became the go-to company for many different organizations. Thanks to the research and development of experimental weaponry and equipment like the flying Raptora armor, they were able to land enough of an Impression to be hired, contracted by the United Nations, as the guard dogs of the many Overwatch facilities that were not in the process of being decommissioned. This relationship led to many dismissing calling this paramilitary "Overwatch 2.0", in spite of critics pointing out how superficial of a difference that truly was.

In spite of that, Helix was able to fill the void left by Overwatch, at least when it came to peacekeeping and guarding important assets, perhaps exemplified best by their assignment on upkeep and defense of the Temple of Anubis in Cairo. Their legitimacy was also boosted by the addition of Fareeha Amari into the Raptora Unit on the Giza Plateau, having been hired fresh out of leaving the army now under the Call sign of "Pharah". Whether the mission is to safely guard the remains of the Naughton Vault at Grand Mesa or deal with escaped experimental Bat-Wolves at Oasis, Helix was always up to the task, bringing justice from above.

events.name: Code of Violence
events.description:
The Zurich explosion had not actually killed off Jack or Gabe, they both vanished after the fact, becoming living ghosts. But Reyes was left in a far worse state, when Talon found his body. Dr. O'Deorain concocted a series of chemicals just to keep him alive, further destabilizing his body's molecular phasing. Reyes was living in a never-ending torment, unable to go back to the world of the living, but all things considered, also unwilling to try.

Having been failed by Overwatch, he decided to give Akande's offer a try, working for Talon alongside another operative, Sombra, to retrieve an asset at a New Mexico site. During the mission, Reyes realized Talon truly lacked any sense of structure, goal or loyalty. Everyone involved was just doing so for their own benefit, loosely fulfilling a shared goal. After clearing off the way into the base, they discovered Subject: Sigma, peacefully floating in maximum security, only to find out an extraction team led by the Widowmaker was to take on the mission from there, as they were still seen as rookies.

This lack of formalities made Reyes wonder what Takin truly was, a means to an end, held together purely by a code of violence. A group of individuals collaborating purely due to twisted desires leading them to work outside the law, and the perfect kind of environment for Reyes to act as judge, jury and executioner, after so many years of red tape getting in the way. Thus, he took on the mantle of the Reaper, wearing a mask to hide his past and becoming a harbinger of death, taking matters into his own hands and forming an expansive target list of individuals he aimed at removing, with the very last names being his Talon coworkers themselves.

Under Talon's care, Sigma enjoyed more freedom than he had for several years. His fractured mind struggled to hold its pieces together, meaning he never truly understood the gravity of his situation working with terrorists, as he no longer saw himself as a prisoner. This, combined with the violent lashing out caused by the maddening melody he heard when his condition distabilized, made him both a complying hostage, and a highly dangerous weapon.

Talon understood Sigma as a human. Flawed, manipulable, and far more useful when willingly cooperating than when forced to. Taking advantage of his vulnerable state, they framed themselves as colleagues and patrons helping him further his research by providing him with everything he needed, when in reality they planned to weaponize both him and the fruits of his research Using their assets. Siebren was slowly able to gain control over his power, allowing gravity to abide by his will, moving closer to his life goal.

But in spite of that, his brittle mind was still unstable. Dr O'Deorain was in charge of supervising his condition and conducted several intrusive tests into his mind to study his condition. During this time, Sombra grew fond of the old man, taking pity on his circumstances and objecting to the way Moira and her scientists treated him. Sombra's kindness played a large role in Sigma's improving mental state, and Talon's continuous indulgence into his fantasies. And since Sombra lacked much loyalty to an organization, it meant now if they ever did something to harm him, they would have to deal with her.

events.name: Shrike
events.description:
Ana has traveled a lot since going off the record, even passing through Junkertown once or twice, getting into brawls with the locals. When she ultimately settled on returning to her homeland, she did so with the intention of finally settling down, living peacefully and quietly. However, as more time passed, she noticed how much her home still struggled to recover.

Even decades later, Anubis' impact could be felt from its throne, as the Crisis left Egypt in ruin and too unstable to fully heal. Ana felt that Overwatch could have done more to help Cairo, and marked them as responsible for many of the problems plaguing the city. What's more, with them gone, Talon began to take over parts of the city and profit out of the chaos.

Ana could no longer stand on the sidelines after seeing her home succumb to endless tragedy. She took on the name of Shrike and became a ghostly vigilante, looking after her country from the shadows, taking base at a distant necropolis, where she took care of many relics and sent them over to a friend of the Wayfinder, Dr. Hamid Faisal. During her crusade, she would also keep a close eye on her family and close allies, writing many letters to Fareeha trying to explain her absence, but not once did she receive a response.

For years, D.va gathered a reputation for being a merciless opponent who played to win at any cost. As these massive competitive events allowed the people of Korea to keep a sense of normalcy over the continuous rise of the Gwishin, D.va would become a household name among many Koreans and people from all over the world, both from her insane skills and actions per minute rate, as well as thanks to her blossoming streaming career they kick-started from her reputation.

What's more, he would often outright vanish for prolonged periods of time, leaving no clue of where he went, only to suddenly come back when a particular assignment peaked his interest. events.name: Runs in the Family
events.description:
Overwatch's campaigns across America forced many gangs like Deadlock to scale back or lie low, but they never truly went away. And now that Overwatch was gone, it marked the start of a second new West. As gangs struggled in bloodshed and skirmishes to expand their territories once again. Ashe saw an opportunity to grow her influence through the chaos. Thanks to the negotiating tactics she learned from back in the day when she was still meant to take over the family business, she came up with a plan and gathered the heads of the major gangs with a proposal for them to work together, or at least not against each other.

Without having to worry about endless squabbles and with the shared assets of her former rivals, Ashe turned Deadlock from a notorious gang to a multi-state criminal syndicate. With their growth came many prominent new members, like the triplets, P. T, Terran, and Zeke, who quickly became some of Ashe's most notorious henchmen, as well as an Omnic Sniper going by Bars, who grew close both with Ashe and especially B.O.B., who had also undergone many upgrades to his systems to better suit his chassis to this renegade lifestyle. But perhaps the most eventful change in the Deadlock family would come from Frankie and Bez, who decided to get engaged around this period. As Deadlock grew, however, Ashe could still not let go of the missing founder. Even after so many years, Cassidy's betrayal pained her like an open wound, and even when she publicly trashed him, deep down she missed him enough to keep photos of them together on her holobike.

Without being able to rely on any system, Findlay was forced to find help outside the law to improve his condition. While researching ways to improve his prosthetics, he came across the Phreaks and their illegal body modding community, so he set out to look for the local cell in Scotland.

The group he found happened to be the home of one of the most prominent members, Touch up, who upgraded him with cutting-edge cybernetics that allowed him to regain mobility and manage the pain better. While he stayed with the Phreaks he got to meet many like-minded individuals, like Jackdaw, Boomslang and the Omnics Revel and Susannah, and over time he began to see them as a newly found family of his, even starting to date Susie.

Now as a fully fledged member, Findlay left his old life behind and adopted the new name of Hazard. Fully committed to the Phreaks' cause of tearing the system down and fighting the organization that perpetrated the broken status quo, he continued upgrading himself with further cybernetic augments, and began to travel around the world, quickly becoming one of the Phreaks' most prominent and radicalized members, Passionately helping other Phreaks and fellow rebels like the Deadlock gang, which commonly stole from large weapon empires like Arbalest and was willing to provide the Phreaks with firepower if they were able to met her price.
